findings.reason: the node is told to lift a head-and-tail helper "both call"; unless the plan states the cut is parameterised (service-log caller keeps zero head bytes), the node will either be unable to give the run file its head+tail or regress the service log.
findings.text: §4 says "the head-and-tail truncation behind the service-log bound ... is lifted into one helper both call", but the cited `trim_service_log` (`reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:548-574`, keyed by `SERVICE_LOG_LIMIT_BYTES`/`SERVICE_LOG_KEEP_BYTES at line 223) keeps only the newest bytes and drops the oldest — it is a tail-only cut, not head-and-tail — so one head-and-tail helper cannot serve both the service log and the run file without changing the service-log behaviour its own tests pin

findings.reason: a "size limit" that can enlarge the file it bounds must tie the kept size to the limit (for example keep = limit/2); the node needs that spec decision to make the measure hold for a small limit.
findings.text: §4 replaces an oversized file with "its first and last megabyte", a fixed 1 MB keep decoupled from the configured limit, so a file whose size sits between the limit and twice the keep is replaced by its overlapping halves plus the marker and does not shrink (a 1.5 MB log under a 1 MB limit becomes ~1.5 MB + marker); the done-when's 1 MB limit with a 3 MB file never exercises this and cannot distinguish keep = 1 MB from keep = limit

findings.reason: a line citation to the wrong construct is the "worse than none" case this item checks; correcting it to `runs.py:3927` is a one-line plan fix and restores consistency with the plan's other definition-line citations.
findings.text: the anchor `runs.py:3985` is cited as the home of `WATCH_LOG_MAX_BYTES`, but the constant is defined at `runs.py:3927`; line 3985 is a continuation line inside the `_WatchLogStream` docstring, so the citation names the class that uses the constant rather than the constant
